findings.checklist_item: - [ ] List `_commands/claim.py` (`claim --review`) and `_commands/composer_edit.py` (`edit --review`) as callers of `_render_plan_review_text` that inherit the new lines, and say whether that is intended.
evidence: claim.py:93: `from rebar._cli._llm_commands import _disposition_exit_code, _render_plan_review_text` then `_render_plan_review_text(result)`
composer_edit.py:480-482: same import and call after `llm.review_plan(resolved, sign=True, repo_root=repo_root)`
Plan scope sentence covers only `--output=text` (the default an operator reads) for `rebar review-plan`; neither claim nor edit is mentioned
findings.finding: `_render_plan_review_text` is shared with two callers outside `_cli/` that the plan doesn't list: `src/rebar/_commands/claim.py` (`_review_before_claim`, used by `rebar claim --review`) and `src/rebar/_commands/composer_edit.py` (the `--review` path after an edit). Both call `llm.review_plan(...)` and pass the result to `_render_plan_review_text`, so they will also start printing the new `model did not run:` / `build drift:` lines. The plan's Context and ACs only describe `rebar review-plan --output=text`.
scenarios: `rebar claim <id> --review` against an attested config whose model id is invalid now prints the build-drift remedy above the 'claim not attempted' error. This is probably wanted, but the plan doesn't say so.
An existing claim/edit text-output test that captures stdout on a degraded review could start seeing the extra lines.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one sentence to Approach step 1: "`_render_plan_review_text` is also used by `rebar claim --review` (`_commands/claim.py`) and `rebar edit --review` (`_commands/composer_edit.py`); they inherit the two lines on degraded results, which is intended."

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In Approach step 2, note that `message_for(CHANGE_SETTINGS)` is also shown by the completion close-gate hint (`completion_verifier_run._failure_hint`) and the review-code degrade line, and confirm the new wording is right for those surfaces.
evidence: completion_verifier_run.py:44-48: `message = failure.message_for(outcome.resolution_class.value, ...)`; `hint = f" [{outcome.resolution_class.value}: {message}]"`
_llm_commands.py:95-109: `_disposition_exit_code` notes that it also handles the code-review review_result, and it writes `llm-degrade: {rc} — {msg}`
Plan step 2 only says the message is printed on the plan-review stderr degrade line
findings.finding: `message_for` has consumers outside the review-plan stderr line that the plan doesn't list. `src/rebar/_commands/completion_verifier_run.py::_failure_hint` builds the `rebar close` completion-gate hint from it (`[CHANGE_SETTINGS: <message>]`). `_disposition_exit_code` and `_llm_error_exit_code` in `_llm_commands.py` also feed the review-code gate's `llm-degrade:` line. So the reworded CHANGE_SETTINGS text will appear on the close and code-review surfaces too, while the plan only talks about the plan-review stderr line.
scenarios: `rebar close` on a ticket whose completion verifier hits a 401 or a max_tokens bound now shows the reworded credentials/model-id/bounds hint.
A max_tokens/length CHANGE_SETTINGS outcome (pinned in `test_plan_review_agentic_verdict.py`) gets the broader text everywhere.
findings.suggested_fix: Append to Approach step 2: "The message is shared by every gate surface (`rebar review-plan`, `review-code`, and the `rebar close` completion hint in `_commands/completion_verifier_run.py`); the new wording is correct for all of them because classification is unchanged."

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the default when `llm_error` is absent and how newlines are handled, and add tests asserting the 300-char truncation and the missing-`llm_error` case.
evidence: "it prints `  model did not run: <coverage.llm_error, first 300 chars>` (when present)"
No AC asserts truncation or the missing-llm_error case.
findings.finding: The `model did not run:` line has gaps in specified behavior and test coverage. The 300-char truncation of `llm_error` has no covering AC or test. The behavior when `llm_ran` is false but `llm_error` is absent is hedged as '(when present)' without saying whether the line prints with no message or is suppressed. Multi-line provider messages are not addressed.
scenarios: A provider returns a long or multi-line error body; the text output spills or the truncation is silently dropped.
A degraded result carries llm_ran=false with no llm_error; the implementer prints a dangling 'model did not run: None' or nothing.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify: when llm_ran is False and llm_error is missing, print '  model did not run' with no message. Collapse newlines in llm_error to spaces before truncating to 300 chars. Add one test with a >300-char error asserting the printed message length and one test with no llm_error.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that `llm_error` is collapsed to one line (newlines → spaces), skipped when empty or whitespace, and suffixed with an ellipsis when truncated at 300 chars, with a test case.
evidence: "it prints `  model did not run: <coverage.llm_error, first 300 chars>` (when present)"
No mention of newline collapsing, an empty-string error, or a truncation indicator.
findings.finding: The `model did not run:` line embeds raw provider text truncated to 300 characters, but the plan does not say how a multi-line or whitespace-only `llm_error` is rendered. It also does not say whether a marker is shown when the text is truncated. Provider exception strings (e.g. Bedrock ValidationException bodies) commonly contain newlines, which would break the indented one-line report format.
findings.location: Approach step 1 (`model did not run: <coverage.llm_error, first 300 chars>`)
scenarios: A provider error containing embedded newlines spills unindented lines into the PLAN REVIEW text block.
An `llm_error` of '' or whitespace prints a bare `model did not run:` label.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Print the `build drift:` line only for a provider-error degrade (`llm_ran is False` and `llm_error` present, or `llm_unavailable`), and add a test that a reused PASS / DET BLOCK carrying `build_drift` but no `llm_error` prints no remedy line.
evidence: Plan: "When `coverage.build_drift` is a dict with a `remedy`, it prints `  build drift: <remedy>`. A clean run (`llm_ran` true or absent) prints neither line."

src/rebar/llm/gate_source.py:268 — `if not isinstance(coverage, dict) or coverage.get("llm_ran") is not False: return` is the only check; despite its docstring, nothing tests whether the verdict is signed.
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/reuse.py:168 — the reused signed PASS sets `coverage = {"llm_ran": False, "idempotent_skip": True}`.
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py:182 — a DET-floor BLOCK sets `llm_ran: False` with no `llm_error`.
src/rebar/llm/build_drift.py:233-236 — the note exists for the case where the provider rejects the request, i.e. the `llm_error` path.
gate_source.py:147 — `warn_if_behind` runs on every attested handle, so `_FOUND` is filled for every gate run on a drifted build.
findings.finding: The planned `build drift:` line prints whenever `coverage.build_drift` has a `remedy`. Upstream, `_note_build_drift` adds that field to every verdict with `llm_ran is False`, not only the case where the provider rejected the request. On a drifted build the text report would show 'update the checkout … run `make install`, then re-run the gate' on a signed reused PASS, a DET BLOCK, a not-claimable fast-fail and a config fault. In none of those did drift cause the model to skip, and on a PASS there is nothing to re-run.
scenarios: An operator on a build 2 commits behind re-runs review-plan on an unchanged ticket and gets `PLAN REVIEW: PASS … reused …` followed by `build drift: … then re-run the gate`.
A plan the DET floor blocks shows the build-drift remedy next to real DET BLOCK findings, which suggests the drift caused the BLOCK.
findings.suggested_fix: In `_render_model_never_ran`, return early unless `coverage.get("llm_ran") is False and coverage.get("llm_error")`, and print both lines under that one condition. Add a case to tests/unit/test_llm_commands_render.py: `{"llm_ran": False, "idempotent_skip": True, "build_drift": {...}}` prints neither line.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reword the CHANGE_SETTINGS message so it does not claim a provider rejection (UserError is raised client-side), e.g. "The request was rejected because of a setting …".
evidence: Plan: "reword … to cover what the class actually holds: \"The provider rejected the request because of a setting (credentials, the model id, or a request parameter …)\""
Plan Context: "`classify_llm_failure` maps pydantic-ai `UserError` there too"
src/rebar/llm/failure.py:304-305 — `if isinstance(exc, UserError): return ResolutionClass.CHANGE_SETTINGS`.
findings.finding: The new CHANGE_SETTINGS message begins "The provider rejected the request". The plan itself notes that `classify_llm_failure` also sends pydantic-ai `UserError` to this class, and that error is raised on the client before any request reaches a provider (for example an unknown model prefix or bad agent arguments). The new wording would be wrong for that path, so it does not fully meet its own goal of covering "what the class actually holds".
scenarios: A local misconfiguration raises `UserError` before any network call, and stderr says the provider rejected the request, sending the operator to the provider console instead of their local config.
findings.suggested_fix: Use: "The request was rejected because of a setting (credentials, the model id, or a request parameter such as a token/step/timeout bound) — check the configured model, credentials and bounds, then retry."

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether the `build drift:` line depends on `llm_ran is False` or prints whenever `build_drift.remedy` exists, and add an AC/test for the `llm_ran: true` + `build_drift` combination.
evidence: "When `coverage.build_drift` is a dict with a `remedy`, it prints `  build drift: <remedy>`."
"A clean run (`llm_ran` true or absent) prints neither line."
AC3 only covers `llm_ran` true AND no `build_drift`, so the conflicting combination is never pinned.
findings.finding: The plan gives two conflicting rules for when the `build drift:` line prints when `build_drift` is present but `llm_ran` is true. Approach item 1 prints it whenever `coverage.build_drift` is a dict with a `remedy`, regardless of `llm_ran`. The next sentence says a clean run (`llm_ran` true or absent) prints neither line.
scenarios: A future or current code path attaches build_drift to a verdict where the model did run (drift present but the gate succeeded); one implementer gates the line on llm_ran, another does not.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the build-drift line independent of llm_ran: the remedy is useful whenever drift is detected. Reword the clean-run sentence to 'a result with llm_ran true/absent and no build_drift prints neither line', and add a test where llm_ran is true and build_drift is present to pin the chosen behavior.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add one test that renders the real degraded verdict (as built in `test_build_drift_degraded_verdict.py`) through `_render_plan_review_text` and asserts the `build drift:` and `model did not run:` lines.
evidence: "proved by a new test in `tests/unit/test_llm_commands_render.py`"
`tests/unit/test_build_drift_degraded_verdict.py` is run but not tied to the text renderer.
VERIFY-COMMAND taxonomy (4) fixture invalidity: a hand-built fixture may not match the produced shape.
findings.finding: The render tests use hand-built `coverage` dicts, so they cannot catch the renderer reading keys or a shape the real degraded verdict does not produce, for example `build_drift` nested differently or coverage being an object rather than a dict. The shape is only confirmed by the manual reproduction, not by a test that chains the real producer into `_render_plan_review_text`.
scenarios: The producer emits `coverage.build_drift` under a key or type the helper does not check (e.g. `isinstance(..., dict)` fails on a model object), so text output stays silent in production while unit tests pass.
findings.suggested_fix: In test_llm_commands_render.py, reuse the degraded-verdict construction from test_build_drift_degraded_verdict.py (or its fixture/helper). Pass its output to _render_plan_review_text and assert that 'build drift:' and 'make install' appear in the captured text.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether `build drift:` prints independently of `llm_ran` or only when `llm_ran is False`, and add an AC/test for the `llm_ran` true + `build_drift` present case.
evidence: "When `coverage.build_drift` is a dict with a `remedy`, it prints `  build drift: <remedy>`."
"A clean run (`llm_ran` true or absent) prints neither line."
AC3: "A result with `llm_ran` true and no `build_drift` prints neither line" — the llm_ran-true-with-build_drift cell is untested.
findings.finding: The rendering rule for the `build drift:` line is internally inconsistent. Step 1 makes it conditional only on `coverage.build_drift` being a dict with a `remedy`. The same step then says 'A clean run (llm_ran true or absent) prints neither line.' It is unspecified whether build_drift is printed when `llm_ran` is true or absent, and AC3 tests only `llm_ran` true with no build_drift, so the case is never pinned.
scenarios: A result where the model ran but coverage still carries build_drift: the implementer may print the drift line (contradicting 'neither line') or suppress it (hiding a real build skew), and no test decides which.
findings.suggested_fix: Decide explicitly, e.g. 'print `build drift:` whenever build_drift has a remedy, regardless of llm_ran'. Reword the clean-run sentence to 'a result with llm_ran true/absent and no build_drift prints neither line', and add a test for llm_ran true + build_drift.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] List the consumers of `message_for`/`RESOLUTION_MESSAGES[CHANGE_SETTINGS]` (stderr degrade line, any JSON/MCP/doc surface) and add a step to update existing tests and docs asserting the old wording; qualify the 'JSON unchanged' claim accordingly.
evidence: "reword `RESOLUTION_MESSAGES[CHANGE_SETTINGS]` …"
"JSON output is unchanged."
Testing section adds only a new assertion; there is no step to locate and modify existing assertions on the old message.
findings.finding: Rewording `RESOLUTION_MESSAGES[CHANGE_SETTINGS]` changes text shown on every path that calls `message_for`. Today that includes the stderr `llm-degrade:` line, and possibly other surfaces such as MCP/JSON payloads or docs. The plan neither enumerates those consumers nor plans to update existing tests or docs that assert the old 'exceeded a configured bound' wording. It also asserts 'JSON output is unchanged' without confirming the message is absent from JSON coverage.
scenarios: An existing test asserting 'tokens/steps/timeout' in the CHANGE_SETTINGS message goes red and is patched ad hoc during `make verify`.
If the resolution message is serialized into coverage or MCP output, the 'JSON unchanged' claim is false and downstream consumers see changed text unannounced.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to Testing: grep tests/ and docs/ for 'configured bound' / 'tokens/steps/timeout' and update those assertions. State whether the resolution message appears in JSON/MCP output.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an AC that re-runs the documented reproduction in `--output=text` and confirms the `build drift:` (with `make install`), `model did not run:` and reworded `llm-degrade:` lines appear.
evidence: The Context documents an exact reproduction, but the ACs cite only `tests/unit/test_llm_commands_render.py` and `test_llm_disposition_plumbing.py`.
No before/after re-run of the reproduction is listed.
findings.finding: Value validation relies only on unit tests over hand-built result dicts. No AC re-runs the plan's own reproduction (wrong Bedrock model id, config 2 commits ahead, `rebar review-plan <id> --ref <sha>` in default text mode) to confirm the operator now sees the drift remedy, the provider error and the corrected stderr message end to end.
scenarios: The real coverage object reaching `_render_plan_review_text` differs from the fabricated test dict (key name, or object vs dict), so unit tests pass while the operator's text output is still missing the lines.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC: 'Re-running the 2026-11-13 reproduction with default text output shows `build drift: … make install …`, `model did not run: … model identifier is invalid`, and the reworded CHANGE_SETTINGS stderr line.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make `_render_model_never_ran` gate-agnostic (read only `result['coverage']`) and call it from the verify-completion and review-code text output too, or from the shared `_disposition_exit_code` seam, or else state explicitly why only plan review is in scope.
evidence: Plan: "add a helper `_render_model_never_ran(result)` called from `_render_plan_review_text`"
Ticket ac3b description: "A gate (`review-plan`, `verify-completion`) reads its `[tool.rebar.llm]` model config from the attested snapshot root"
src/rebar/llm/completion.py:250 and src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py:607,623,634 call `gate_source.annotate_result`, so completion and code-review verdicts get `build_drift` too.
search_files('llm_ran', src/rebar/_cli) → (no matches): no text renderer shows the field for any gate.
src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py:95-109 — `_disposition_exit_code` is the shared seam that already writes the `llm-degrade:` line from `coverage`.
findings.finding: The fix only touches plan review, but the hidden-remedy defect affects every gate. The source bug (ac3b) names `review-plan` and `verify-completion`, and `gate_source.annotate_result` adds `build_drift` to completion (completion.py:250) and code-review (gate_dispatch.py:607-634) verdicts too. No CLI text renderer reads `llm_ran`/`llm_error`/`build_drift`. A better design is a gate-agnostic helper that reads only `result['coverage']`, called from each gate's text output, or from the shared `_disposition_exit_code` seam, which already prints the `llm-degrade:` line for every gate. That fixes all gates with the same number of lines and tests.
findings.location: Approach step 1 / Context: "attaches `coverage.build_drift` … to a gate verdict whose model never ran"
scenarios: `rebar verify-completion <id>` from a stale worktree still prints only an INDETERMINATE verdict and the misleading CHANGE_SETTINGS line, with no build-drift remedy, which is exactly how the original bug was observed.
